source.section: PDF p.14 Line 8; PDF p.15 Line 15 (Tier 1 benefits on line 8, Social Security on line 15, both subtracted); PDF p.16 Line 22 and PDF p.17 qualified income; Form ND-1 lines 1b, 4b, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25; booklet PDF p.4 (starting point is federal taxable income), PDF p.13 Line 1b, PDF p.16 Line 20, PDF p.29 Tax Rate Schedules, PDF pp.22-28 Tax Table

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = IRA distribution (person 1) 150,000.00 + railroad retirement (Tier 2, taxed federally as a pension) (person 0) 18,000.00 + taxable Social Security 27,200.00 = 195,200.00. Taxable Social Security 27,200.00 is the federal amount given (gross 32,000.00). Federal taxable income = 195,200.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 2 x 1,600.00 age 65 additional = 160,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form ND-1 line 1b federal taxable income 160,500.00; lines 2-3 additions 0.00, line 4a 0.00; line 4b = 160,500.00. Subtractions: line 8 U.S. Railroad Retirement Board benefits 18,000.00; line 15 Social Security benefit exclusion, the taxable amount on Form 1040 line 6b, 27,200.00. Line 17 total subtractions = 45,200.00. Line 18 North Dakota taxable income = 160,500.00 - 45,200.00 = 115,300.00. Line 19 = 115,300.00. Line 20 tax: 1.95% x (115,300.00 - 80,975.00) = 1.95% x 34,325.00 = 669.3375, to the cent 669.34; taxable income is 100,000 or more, so the form itself uses the schedule (PDF p.29). Lines 21-23 credits: line 22 marriage penalty credit: qualified income after lines 8 and 15 is 0.00 and 150,000.00; the lower is not more than 47,550.00, so none. Expected credits 0.00. Line 25 net tax = 669.34. All the Social Security here is SSA-1099 benefit, so all of it goes on line 15; were part of it Tier 1, the line 8 and line 15 split by gross benefits would change the two lines and not their total.
